response:
The changes form one coherent feature with no own-branch bug fixes to elide. Here is the squash commit message:

feat(CC-0114): seed K-ORC bootstrap clouds.yaml from operator

- Add `seedBootstrapCloudsYAML` to the c5c3-operator's `reconcileKORC`:
  it writes the password-based admin clouds.yaml into the
  `{cp.Name}-admin-app-credential` Secret's `clouds.yaml` key with
  write-if-empty semantics, breaking the AdminCredentialReady
  chicken-and-egg deadlock on a fresh cluster without any external shell
  seed. Once the application credential is minted the seed is a no-op and
  never clobbers the minted document; after a re-mint drops the key it
  re-seeds the password version to bridge re-authentication.
- Add `ensureKORCCloudsYAMLExternalSecret`: the operator now creates and
  owns a per-ControlPlane `k-orc-clouds-yaml` ExternalSecret in the CR's
  child namespace (co-located with the K-ORC CRs per C1), reading the
  per-CR OpenBao path `adminAppCredentialRemoteKeyFor(cp)` with
  `creationPolicy: Owner`, hourly refresh, and a controller owner
  reference for GC — so an arbitrarily named ControlPlane resolves to the
  correct key with no manifest edit.
- Wire the seed, the backup PushSecret that mirrors it to OpenBao, and
  the per-CR ExternalSecret into `reconcileKORC` before the credential is
  minted, each guarded with its own KORCReady failure reason
  (`SeedCloudsYamlError`, `PushSecretError`, `ExternalSecretError`).
- Remove `seed_korc_bootstrap_clouds_yaml` and its per-identity
  invocation from `write-bootstrap-secrets.sh`; the script now seeds only
  the per-ControlPlane Model B admin password.
- Drop the `KORC_KEYSTONE_AUTH_URL` export from `deploy-infra.sh`; the
  operator derives the in-cluster Keystone auth URL per CR, so the shell
  stack no longer seeds the clouds.yaml or overrides the auth URL.
- Reduce `deploy/eso/externalsecrets/k-orc-clouds-yaml.yaml` to only the
  static `orc-system` copy backing K-ORC's global default clouds.yaml
  mount; the control-plane-namespace ExternalSecret is now
  operator-created per CR.
- Replace the old fresh-cluster deadlock unit test with tests covering
  `seedBootstrapCloudsYAML` (write-if-empty, no overwrite of minted
  clouds.yaml, repopulation after re-mint, internal endpoint type and
  projected per-CR auth_url) and `ensureKORCCloudsYAMLExternalSecret`
  (shape, owner reference, per-CR remote key, idempotent no-churn), plus
  `reconcileKORC` edge cases (defer before seeding when the admin
  password is missing, steady-state non-overwrite).
- Update the envtest integration test to assert the operator creates the
  per-CR ExternalSecret (owner reference, per-CR remoteRef.key) rather
  than pre-creating it, then simulate its ESO sync.
- Update the c5c3 E2E suites to wait for the operator-owned ExternalSecret
  instead of pre-creating it: add a `wait_ready_condition` helper and
  assert per-CR ownership and remoteRef.key for both tenants in the
  multi-controlplane test, widening its sequential timeout budget.
- Update the quick-start, CRD, reconciler, and infrastructure reference
  docs to describe the operator-owned bootstrap seed and per-CR
  ExternalSecret, and drop the now-unnecessary manual ExternalSecret
  force-sync step.
